column2: Breath retention and forceful practices alter blood pressure and CO2 levels
Breathing techniques affect heart rate and blood pressure
Breath retention and rapid breathing significantly impact BP
Rapid or forceful breathing can trigger symptoms
Strain on compromised respiratory system
Hyperventilation and breath holds can trigger episodes
Breath retention increases intraocular pressure
Breathing techniques stress surgical sites
Forceful exhalation (like Kapalbhati) aggravates condition
Some breath retention practices can trigger anxiety symptoms
Impaired judgment and altered breathing response
Stop immediately if dizzy, light-headed, tingly, short of breath, nauseous, chest pain, or racing heart.
Practice seated or lying down in a safe, stable position — never while standing in an unsafe place.
Never practice while driving, operating machinery, swimming, or in water.
Breathe gently without strain. Mild effort is normal; discomfort is a signal to stop.
Practice on a relatively empty stomach (wait 2–3 hours after a heavy meal).
Children should practice only with adult supervision, and only gentle techniques.
Progress gradually — do not exceed recommended rounds or durations, especially as a beginner.
6 min · Gentle
Gentlest technique. If slowing breath increases anxiety, stop and rest. Not for panic disorder without professional guidance.
Inhale 4s · Hold 7s · Exhale 8s
7-second hold can cause light-headedness. Limit to 4 rounds. Not recommended without medical guidance if pregnant, high BP, or severe respiratory illness.
Inhale 4s · Hold 4s · Exhale 4s · Hold 4s
Two breath holds per cycle. If empty-lung hold causes anxiety, skip it. Blood pressure and pregnancy cautions apply.
Alternate Nostril · Gentle
Avoid if sinus infection, cold, or flu (congestion causes strain). Use light finger pressure only. Keep breath silent and smooth.
Rapid forceful exhales · Advanced

MOST INTENSE technique. DO NOT practice if pregnant, menstruating, heart disease, high BP, hernia, epilepsy, vertigo, glaucoma, recent surgery, panic/anxiety. Over-breathing causes dizziness — stop if tingly. Empty stomach only.

Breathing practices can bring up strong emotions or, rarely, panic or dissociation. Karmana AI Companion is a supportive tool, NOT a therapist or crisis service. If in emotional distress, contact a mental-health professional or local emergency/crisis helpline immediately.
